general_symptoms: Large brown spots with target-like concentric rings on leaves
Fruit becomes mummified and hard
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Apply fungicides containing myclobutanil or propiconazole during the growing season.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Prune for air circulation, remove infected plant parts, and ensure proper spacing.

general_symptoms: Dark brown to black lesions on young berries, resembling measles
Leaves may show yellowing and browning between veins
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).cause: Fungal complex including Phaeomoniella chlamydospora and Phaeoacremonium aleophilum
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: No effective chemical control; focus on cultural practices.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Avoid wounding vines during pruning, use clean tools, and plant resistant varieties if available.

general_symptoms: Small, dark brown spots with yellow halos on leaves
Spots can coalesce and cause significant defoliation
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Use protective fungicides like mancozeb or copper-based products.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Improve air circulation through pruning and avoid overhead irrigation.

general_symptoms: No visible signs of disease
Green, full leaves without spots or discoloration
Grape___healthy.treatment: Maintain good vineyard hygiene and standard care practices.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Regular monitoring and preventive cultural practices.

general_symptoms: Olive-green to black, velvety spots on leaves and fruit
Leaves may become distorted or yellow and drop early
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Apply fungicides containing myclobutanil, captan, or sulfur during the spring.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, rake and remove fallen leaves, and prune for air flow.

general_symptoms: Purple or brown spots on leaves that turn black
Fruit develops sunken, black, rotten areas ('frog-eye' spots)
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Use fungicides like captan or thiophanate-methyl during bloom and fruit development.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Remove infected plant debris, prune out cankers, and maintain good air circulation.

general_symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on top of leaves
Orange, gelatinous, horn-like structures may appear on the undersides of leaves
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Fungus Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae, requires both apple and cedar/juniper hosts
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Apply protective fungicides containing myclobutanil or propiconazole.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Remove nearby cedar or juniper trees if possible, or choose resistant apple varieties.

general_symptoms: No visible signs of disease
Green, full leaves without spots or discoloration
Apple___healthy.treatment: Maintain good orchard hygiene and standard care practices.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Regular monitoring and preventive cultural practices.

general_symptoms: Small, dark spots with concentric rings (target spots) on older leaves
Leaves may yellow and die from the bottom up
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or copper compounds.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops, plant resistant varieties, avoid overhead watering, and ensure good air circulation.

general_symptoms: Water-soaked, dark green to brown spots on leaves, often starting at leaf tips or edges
White fungal growth may appear on the undersides of leaves under humid conditions
Rapid wilting and death of foliage
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply systemic fungicides like metalaxyl or mancozeb immediately.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, ensure good air flow, avoid overhead watering, and monitor weather conditions closely.

Potato___healthy.treatment: Maintain good field hygiene and standard care practices.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Regular monitoring and preventive cultural practices.
